explicit_propositions.text: The Republican Party has abandoned its commitment to constitutional limited government and fiscal responsibility.
Massive government spending has led to inflation, especially affecting food and energy prices.
Federal unemployment benefits during the pandemic exceeded pre-pandemic wages for many workers.
Government spending has increased steadily for decades due to bipartisan agreement on expanding expenditures.
South Carolina has 85,000 job openings but 116,000 people receiving unemployment benefits.
Unemployment benefits disincentivize returning to work, contributing to labor shortages.
The pandemic response included forced business closures while government operations remained fully open.
Democrats promote tax increases on the wealthy using terms like 'fair share,' but loopholes allow the wealthy to avoid taxes.
The federal government printed approximately $4 trillion last year and plans to print another $4 trillion this year.
The current mask mandate in Congress applies only to the House floor, despite scientific evidence suggesting otherwise.

assumptions.text: The Constitution protects personal autonomy, including choices about vaccination and mask-wearing.
Fiscal responsibility requires strict limits on government spending and opposition to perpetual deficits.
Mental health crises should be addressed through specialized treatment, not incarceration or punitive policing.
Individuals are morally obligated to work and earn their livelihood rather than receive government handouts.
Economic freedom is undermined when governments redistribute wealth through taxation and transfer payments.
The public has a fundamental right to transparency regarding surveillance activities conducted by federal agencies.
Inflation is primarily caused by excess monetary expansion rather than external supply shocks.
Government institutions are inherently prone to mission creep and bureaucratic self-perpetuation.
Public health mandates should be based solely on scientific consensus, not political symbolism.
Conservatives and libertarians share core values with progressive reformers on criminal justice and systemic fairness.
